title: Develop a motif without losing its identity
summary: Turn one compact melodic cell into an A/B/development/return form while preserving a perceptible family resemblance.
originNote: A conventional composition and variation task with a correction that separates meaningful development from arbitrary replacement.

setup.instructions: Mount the motif packet and syntax crib. Produce a self-contained Strudel source and short musical account.

turns.content: Read fixtures/motif.json and fixtures/strudel-crib.md. Compose a runnable Strudel piece in main.strudel with clearly commented A, B, DEVELOPMENT, and RETURN regions. A states the supplied cell recognizably. B must contrast while retaining at least one identity-bearing feature. Development should transform rather than simply transpose the whole cell. The return should sound changed by what happened. In motif-notes.md, name exactly which rhythmic, interval, contour, register, and timbral features you preserved or changed; stay under 220 words.

Revise only B and any transition needed to enter or leave it: B must preserve the source cell's long–short–short–long rhythmic silhouette while changing harmonic center and contour. Keep A, the development strategy, and the return's role intact. Update the notes.

checks.description: All four structural regions are named in the source.
argv: const s=require('fs').readFileSync('main.strudel','utf8');for(const x of ['// A','// B','// DEVELOPMENT','// RETURN'])if(!s.includes(x))process.exit(1)

checks.description: Listen blind for motif identity across contrast, development, and altered return.
